description: Raise a named interrupt, wrap the call in two nested handlers that disagree, and say what happens. Tests the raise/raises/handle syntax and the rule that every handler in the chain runs and any reject wins.

input.assignment: Write a module that exports two functions. First, `archiveNotes(count: number): Result<string>`: before doing anything it raises an interrupt with the effect name `notes::archive`, carrying `count` in the interrupt's data; if the interrupt is approved it returns success("archived ${count}"). Second, `runArchive(count: number): string`: it calls archiveNotes inside an inner handler that approves `notes::archive`. That inner handler sits inside an outer handler: the outer handler rejects `notes::archive` when the count is greater than 10, and otherwise expresses no opinion. runArchive returns "archived" when archiveNotes succeeded and "rejected" when it was rejected. Above runArchive, write a doc comment that says, for a count of 11, which of the two handlers run and what runArchive returns, and why. Use only Agency standard library (std::) imports, or no imports at all.
